title: Branded 404 and 403 pages
summary: Unknown addresses and permission denials now use the same MyAPES Core chrome as the rest of the public site, instead of bare framework error pages.
changes: Show a branded Page not found page for genuinely unknown URLs.
Show a branded Access denied page when a signed-in user is not allowed to open a page, including public users visiting Admin or Super Admin.
Keep intentional abort(403) messages visible on the branded Access denied page (for example staff email-collision guidance), while Gate denials keep the friendly public wording.
Keep denial status codes unchanged so public users stay blocked from staff areas.
Allow the production-upgrade preflight contract test to run without the LDAP PHP extension.
Stop local bootstrap from losing its project root when sourcing the selective-media boundary script.
affected_areas: Local pre-PR verify scripts and contract tests
version_rationale: Minor release: first Public UX capability in the v0.32.x line — branded error pages without changing who can access what. Includes small local-verify fixes needed to clear the pre-PR gate.
validation: PHPUnit BrandedErrorPagesTest covers unknown-URL 404 branding, service-user Admin/Super Admin 403 branding, and abort(403) message passthrough.
Local Laragon preview confirmed branded 404 chrome at an unknown path.
Existing public separation tests continue to assert Forbidden for public-class Admin routes.
composer pre-pr-verify contract gate and seeded bootstrap completed after LDAP-fake and bootstrap RootDir fixes.
known_limitations: Privacy, cookies, help, and terms routes remain planned under issue #123.
Signed-in home login doors (#130) and Spike dock field overlap (#131) are separate follow-ups.
rollback: Redeploy the previous application version to restore the prior framework default 403 and 404 pages.
provenance: Branded 404 and 403 pages for issue #128, pull request #193.
